safety.confidence_note: Study date not given in the review; 2012 is a proxy for IND-enabling work before ozanimod's first-in-human study (Tran 2017).
safety.note: IND-enabling monkey CV study: ozanimod cut heart rate 20% and diastolic pressure 20% at the top dose.
safety.quote: Heart rate decreased by 20% and the R-R interval increased by 37% at the highest dose given and persisted for 24 hours after dosing.
safety.judgement: Opener at a proxy first-use year; the study is only public through the 2020 review.

safety.magnitude_basis: first-dose heart rate fall; diastolic BP fell in monkeys but rose in patients
safety.confidence_note: Comparison made in the MS NDA (patients with relapsing MS); grep of the summary review only, the pharm/tox review is not in the bundle.
safety.note: FDA set the monkey heart-rate fall beside patients' bradycardia; the monkeys' diastolic pressure fall was opposite to patients' rise.
safety.short: Monkey heart-rate fall seen in patients
safety.quote: Reduction in heart rate and increased blood pressure are seen in patients treated with ozanimod.
safety.reason: Heart rate matched; blood pressure opposite
safety.judgement: Scored same with source_calls_it partial: heart rate matched in direction (the class's main first-dose harm), blood pressure went the other way. Unlike the S1P3-KO mouse, the filed system predicted ozanimod's bradycardia. Imported from MS.

safety.confidence_note: Study date not given; 2014 is a proxy for IND-enabling safety pharmacology before etrasimod's first-in-human studies.
safety.note: Single oral etrasimod doses up to 350 mg/kg had no cardiovascular effect in dogs.
safety.quote: A single oral dose of etrasimod did not produce acute CNS or clinically relevant respiratory effects in rats (NOELs: 350 mg/kg/day) or cardiovascular effects in dogs (NOEL: 350 mg/kg/day).
safety.judgement: Opener at a proxy year; public only through the 2023 review.

safety.magnitude_basis: first-dose heart rate change (dogs none at NOEL 350 mg/kg; UC patients -7.2 bpm)
safety.confidence_note: Whether beagles show S1P1-mediated first-dose bradycardia was not verified; the review places the dog result and the clinical heart-rate fall in one paragraph but does not call the dog study a miss.
safety.note: Dogs showed no cardiovascular effect, yet UC patients' heart rate fell 7.2 bpm after the first 2 mg dose.
safety.short: Dogs silent; patients' heart rate fell
safety.quote: After the first dose of VELSIPITY 2 mg, subjects with UC experienced the greatest mean decrease from baseline in heart rate of 7.2 bpm at Hour 3 in UC-1 and Hour 2 in UC-2.
safety.judgement: Contra: silence on a harm a dog's heart can show (dogs have atrial GIRK channels), at a NOEL far above clinical exposure. Paired within the review, so comparison_stated false. The review credits the human atrial myocyte assay (already in the draft) for the mechanism.

safety.confidence_note: Study date not given; 2014 proxy. Heterologous cell line, coded ex_vivo as the nearest model_kind.
safety.note: Etrasimod had no significant effect on hERG current (59% inhibition at 3 µM, IC50 an estimated 4-12x Cmax).
safety.quote: In a standard battery of nonclinical safety pharmacology studies, etrasimod had no significant effects on hERG channel current in vitro, cardiovascular function in dogs, CNS parameters in rats, or respiratory function in rats.

safety.magnitude_basis: hERG call vs thorough QT result at 4 mg (2x clinical dose)
safety.confidence_note: The review's own estimate puts the hERG IC50 at 4-12x Cmax, below the usual 30x margin, so the assay's 'no significant effect' call is softer than it reads. TQT date and registration not looked up.
safety.note: The thorough QT study found no significant QTc prolongation at a supratherapeutic 4 mg, as the hERG assay predicted.
safety.short: No QTc prolongation, as hERG predicted
safety.quote: In the thorough QT study, etrasimod was not associated with significant QTc prolonging effect at a supratherapeutic dose of 4 mg QD on Day 14
safety.reason: hERG call held in the TQT study
safety.judgement: Off-target safety, single modality so no modality field. Paired within the review (comparison_stated false). Ozanimod's TQT (metabolite CC112273) was also negative but no ozanimod hERG datum was in the bundle.

added_models.model: Rat and monkey repeat-dose toxicology, lung (ozanimod)

safety.confidence_note: Study dates not given; 2012 is a proxy for the IND-enabling toxicology package.
safety.note: Rat and monkey toxicology named the lung a prominent ozanimod target: macrophage infiltration, heavier lungs, faster breathing in rats.
safety.short: Rat and monkey: lung is a target
safety.quote: The lung was a prominent target of ozanimod in rat and monkey.
safety.judgement: Opener at a proxy year; public only through the 2020 review.

safety.magnitude_basis: lung findings in animals vs FEV1 decline in patients
safety.confidence_note: Paired, not stated: FDA based its respiratory concern on prior S1P drugs in humans, not on the animal findings; animal histology (macrophage infiltration) and human spirometry are different readouts.
safety.note: Patients on ozanimod lost FEV1 dose-dependently (60 mL vs interferon at 12 months), as the animal lung findings flagged.
safety.short: Patients' FEV1 fell, as animals flagged
safety.quote: Dose-dependent reductions in absolute forced expiratory volume over 1 second (FEV1) were observed in patients treated with ZEPOSIA as early as 3 months after treatment initiation.
safety.reason: Animal lung target; patient FEV1 fell
safety.judgement: Paired within the same NDA (MS); direction only. Etrasimod's rat lung histiocytosis and its UC-1 FEV1 decline are the same pattern but belong to the draft's rat-dog-tox-etrasimod system, so not added here.

considered_not_added: Etrasimod population PK/PD heart-rate model (ARE0301H-HR, FDA 216956): fit to human phase 1-3 data, used to justify no titration; a model of the patient data, not a preclinical system, so no independent prediction to score.
Multi-species blood lymphocyte EC50 for etrasimod (rat/dog/mouse/monkey, 2.5-4.5x below clinical Cmax): same readout as the draft's mouse-blood-lymphocytes engagement track.
Etrasimod rat lung histiocytosis vs UC-1 FEV1 decline: same system as the draft's rat-dog-tox-etrasimod track (dose cell); left to the drafter rather than opening a duplicate model_id.
CD4+CD45RBhi transfer colitis for etrasimod and IL-10-/- colitis for mocravimod: already tracked (mouse-tnbs-transfer-colitis, il10ko-colitis-mouse).
Patient-derived biopsy tissue-slice cultures (PMID 42329475): tested budesonide and myrrh only, no member drug.
Etrasimod ELEVATE mucosal/blood immunophenotyping (doi 10.1093/ecco-jcc/jjag159): patient biomarker study, no model prediction; lymphocyte fall did not differ between remitters and non-remitters.
Patient-level predictors (S1PR1 expression, genetic variants, organoids, ex vivo sensitivity): none found for a member drug.
Mouse EAE and cuprizone models (ozanimod): MS efficacy, not UC.
Rat/rabbit embryo-fetal toxicity: no patient comparison available.
